components.name: Underline Input
components.description: Floating label, hairline bottom, white line grows on focus.
components.css: .ds-input-wrap { position: relative; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1); } .ds-input-wrap::after { content: ''; position: absolute; bottom: 0; left: 0; height: 1px; width: 0; background: #ffffff; transition: width 0.5s; } .ds-input-wrap:focus-within::after { width: 100%; } .ds-input-underline { width: 100%; background: transparent; border: none; outline: none; padding: 28px 0 12px; color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8); font-family: 'Inter', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; } .ds-input-label { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25); font-family: 'Inter', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; pointer-events: none; transition: all 0.3s; } .ds-input-underline:focus ~ .ds-input-label, .ds-input-underline:not(:placeholder-shown) ~ .ds-input-label { top: 12px; transform: none; font-size: 0.75rem; } .ds-input-wrap:focus-within .ds-input-label { color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45); }

narrative.overview: The site is a stage. The hero drops you into a dark, animated theater: one confident voice in Cormorant Garamond, one spotlight of Signal Orange, and JetBrains Mono stage directions whispering what is happening. The rest of the show alternates acts: dark cinematic surfaces (process, the contact stage) against warm editorial daylight (services, portfolio, the testimonials lounge). Nothing here is a template with a name swapped in. The design itself is the portfolio piece, which is the whole pitch: this is a website that proves the person who built it can build websites. The system explicitly rejects generic SaaS templates (centered hero, three identical feature cards, blue gradient CTA), agency cliche (stock hero photos, "full-service digital agency" filler), portfolio cliche (a grid of identical screenshot cards with no point of view), and plain, forgettable, visually quiet work. Every section funnels toward the contact path while still reading as craft to a hiring manager.
keyCharacteristics: Expressive editorial serif display (Cormorant Garamond) carrying the voice; mono labels annotate the structure
Dark cinematic sections alternate with warm light sections; never a flat single-mood page
One spotlight accent, Signal Orange, used with scarcity
Signature gestures: outlined text strokes, italic serif interjections, inline circular image embeds in the hero
Warm near-blacks everywhere, never pure #000; warm browns in the testimonials lounge

rules.name: The Spotlight Rule
rules.body: Signal Orange appears on no more than 5% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point: when it shows up, it is the only thing asking for the click.

rules.name: The Warm Dark Rule
rules.body: Near-black surfaces are never pure #000. They carry warmth (#0e0e0e, #121212) or brown (#2c1a0e). If a dark surface looks cold, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Mono Annotation Rule
rules.body: Labels, eyebrows, and section markers are always JetBrains Mono, uppercase, tracked wide. Never set a label in the serif. The serif performs, the mono documents.

rules.name: The Unused Font Rule
rules.body: Playfair Display, Bebas Neue, Syne, and Space Grotesk are loaded or declared but used nowhere. Prune them; unused fonts are dead weight on the page.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only where the system names them. If a card needs a shadow to separate from its background, the tonal layering is wrong.

dos: Do set every display and heading in Cormorant Garamond, and every label in JetBrains Mono uppercase with wide tracking.
Do alternate dark cinematic sections with warm light sections; a single-mood page reads as template.
Do keep Signal Orange rare, no more than 5% of any screen.
Do use warm near-blacks (#0e0e0e, #121212, #2c1a0e), never pure #000.
Do keep cards flat with Hairline borders; reserve shadows for the two named cases.
Do give every interactive element a visible focus state, and honor prefers-reduced-motion by calming entrances and pausing the carousel.
Do use the established easing curve cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) with durations between 200ms and 600ms for all motion.
donts: Don't look like a generic SaaS template: no Inter-everything centered hero, no three identical feature cards, no blue gradient CTA.
Don't use agency cliche: no stock hero photos, no "we are a full-service digital agency" filler, no jargon.
Don't use the portfolio cliche: no grid of identical screenshot cards with no point of view. The site must feel authored and expressive.
Don't be plain and boring. If a screen could pass for a default template, it has failed.
Don't use gradient text, side-stripe borders, or decorative glassmorphism.
Don't ship unused fonts (Playfair, Bebas Neue, Syne, Space Grotesk) or reference unloaded fonts (DM Sans). Resolve the font stack.
Don't use pure #000 or #fff for surfaces; tint everything warm.
